entries.subject: Ďurech & Hanuš (2026), model 1 of (21900) Orus: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: Model 1 of the deposit (version 2026-09-17), pole (36.8°, -54°), period 13.486235 h, taken unchanged from shape_models/model_21900_1.tri. The deposit lists two spin solutions with the same period. Solution 1 is selected because its pole lies beside the pole of Mottola et al. (2023), ecliptic (33°, −59°), which the 2021 October 16 occultation told apart from its mirror; the separation of both solutions is in /comparison.

entries.subject: Physical scale
entries.finding: 60 ± 0.9 km, volume-equivalent diameter of the occultation-scaled convex model. Table 3 gives the convex shape volume 1.13 × 10^5 km³ of the model its authors scaled to the 2021 October 16 occultation chords; a sphere of that volume is 60 km across. The quoted error is that of the table's surface-equivalent diameter, 60.5 ± 0.9 km. That model's mesh is not archived, so its volume is given to the Ďurech & Hanuš (2026) mesh, whose proportions differ: at this scale the mesh measures 70.4 × 59.8 × 58.2 km (longest extent across the spin axis, the extent at right angles to it, the extent along it) where the table lists 70.7 × 63 × 51.4 km.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: This review did not locate or qualify reusable imagery registered to the selected reconstruction. Disk-integrated photometry and DAMIT model metadata are not surface maps.
entries.revisitWhen: A released, reusable surface observation or mapped product with registration to this body’s selected source model; the existing grid alone does not imply that every archive was searched.

entries.subject: Lucy mission and model references
entries.finding: The 2025 Lucy mission summary remains a contextual cross-reference. This metadata review did not use it to newly qualify geometry, imagery or rotational phase.

entries.subject: DAMIT model catalogue coverage
entries.finding: The official DAMIT asteroid and model CSV exports read on 2026-10-06 (newest model created 2026-07-29) contain no Orus row. The Ďurech & Hanuš (2026) paper says its models go to DAMIT; until they appear there, the Zenodo deposit is the source.
entries.revisitWhen: A DAMIT export lists Orus with a model id.

entries.subject: PDS SBN catalogue values that disagree with the factsheet or are not shown
entries.finding: Shown size Display reference radius "30 km (size-calibrated model)" (doi-10-3847-psj-acaf79); Published dimensions "70.7 × 63 × 51.4 km" (doi-10-3847-psj-acaf79) differs from the NEOWISE V2.0 neowise_jupiter_trojans.csv record 297 (Grav et al. 2012) diameter 50.810 ± 0.809 km (NEOWISE, NEATM); the shown value is kept.
entries.revisitWhen: A newer release of the named catalogue, or a review that replaces the shown value.
